dse_runs.notes: DDS spec: 1 sample/clock at >=250 MSPS, err <= 2^-13, min LUTs. Pipelined_m (m=1) is the natural family for 1-sample-per-clock; iterative is too slow (12 cycles/sample ~ 83 MSPS at 1GHz). unrolled_k likely area-hungry. Prior calibration: cost model underestimates LUTs ~19%, FFs ~11%, Fmax ~10% vs yosys+nextpnr-xilinx. Favor data_width ~16-18, n_iter ~14-16 for 2^-13 accuracy.

l4: no recorded synthesis for this design (L4 is not run live in campaigns)
final_text:
**Campaign summary — dds_250msps (seed 1):**

The single spec `dds_250msps` (NCO/DDS sin-cos generator, ≥250 MSPS, err ≤ 2⁻¹³, min LUTs) was taken down the full fidelity ladder. L1 exploration consumed all 400 evaluations across four NSGA-II studies: an initial `run_dse` (100 evals) that surfaced the pipelined family as the only viable option for 1-sample-per-clock throughput, followed by three targeted `explore_family` runs narrowing the box to data_width 16–19, n_iter 14–17. The front converged on **`pipelined: data_width=18, n_iter=15, angle_guard=2, frac_guard=0, rounding=round`** — estimated 920 LUTs, 953 FFs, 264 MSPS throughput, max error 2⁻¹³·¹⁷. L3/L4/L5 via the ladder subagent found no recorded verification or synthesis data for this design (no measured LUTs/FFs/Fmax), and `back_annotate` returned `no_measured_data` with no winner change, so no reexplore was needed. The spec was finalized on the estimated-cost selection. A lesson note was stored for future campaigns.
